reviews.verdict: Revisit historical rationale and explicitly settle archive policy; no demonstrated ISO or ratification violation.
reviews.decision_question: Does Table 29 /NeedsRendering alone define the project's dynamic-XFA classification used by archive's default stop gate?
evidence: ADR 2876 accepted 2026-11-13 on A840; current scope-ratifications.md and CLAUDE.md also classify XFA 3.3 template grammar outside XFAF as dynamic
sites::xfa_form_is_dynamic returns true only for catalog /NeedsRendering true
archive prepare rejects XFA removal only when that predicate is true and FormAnswers.remove_dynamic_xfa is false
existing dynamic-XFA test only uses /NeedsRendering true
reviews.reasoning: Current scope includes grammar-dynamic templates, so the old statement that nothing in the file can distinguish the class is obsolete. ADR2876 authorizes/schedules layout; it does not expressly amend the archive refusal predicate. The parent therefore does not make the proposed grammar-only stop expectation a permanent failing test. Keep flag-only handling versus broader grammar detection as a decision to settle, separately from the explicit malformed-preservation contract.

reviews.verdict: retain core mechanism; qualify XFA-specific proof and one input-validation edge
reviews.decision_question: Does archive output actually preserve the replaced XFA bytes and state the required attachment relationship/date/association?
evidence: XFA packet test compares decoded concatenated attachment bytes in source order and checks generic MIME fallback/output target/report
generic XMP attachment test compares original payload bytes and checks Source, Params Size/ModDate, and catalog AF
attach.rs uses one generic associated-file writer for both XFA and XMP
the XFA test itself does not assert Source, ModDate, or AF identity
reviews.reasoning: The shared writer gives credible implementation evidence for Source/ModDate/AF; the XFA test proves its own extraction and byte order. Still, XFA-specific assertion could be strengthened cheaply because it already supplies ModDate and reopens the output. In xfa_resource, array elements resolving to non-stream objects are silently skipped, despite the adjacent refusal text claiming malformed shape/refused resource. This is a malformed-source safeguard gap and data-integrity concern, not a claim that ISO requires rejection of every malformed producer file. Do not state a valid-file nonconformance based on it. The all-or-nothing preservation contract is explicit in ADR 1270 and XFA_NOT_READABLE; malformed arrays should not be partially attached. A negative/positive control draft is available, explicitly classified as a defensive data-integrity test rather than an ISO conformance test.

evidence: A840 accepted 2026-11-13; ADR 2876; scope-ratifications.md §A page laid out by a producer's own XFA template; CLAUDE.md current near-side rule
Annex K shard states dynamic template layout is scheduled after ledger and not yet built

reviews.verdict: draft defensive refusal regression; retain the malformed-input qualification
reviews.decision_question: When operator asks to attach the removed XFA resource, does a malformed packet array fail atomically instead of attaching only streams that happened to decode?
evidence: attach::xfa_resource skips any packet item resolving to a non-stream and continues; it returns Some(out) if any bytes were collected
XFA_NOT_READABLE and ADR 1270 explicitly say a malformed shape/read failure must refuse rather than preserve a part
existing valid packet-array archive test is an exact-byte positive control
reviews.reasoning: This is an internal preservation-integrity promise for malformed input, not a source-mandated reject rule for every PDF reader. The scratch draft expects no partial attachment and uses the existing valid array case as the positive control. Parent may select this robustness contract if it wants the implementation to uphold the refusal reason it already reports.
